Nurul Amin, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Mazibar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent Nos.1-7 
For Respondent Nos.8-24 ------ None represented

Mohizuddin and others ------ Petitioners

Abdul Latif and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J. This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 20th day of March, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1106 of 2006 making the Rule absolute thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 09.01.2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No.241 of 2004 who allowed the title appeal thereby reversing those dated 13.10.2004 by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.17 of 2004 decreeing the suit. 

 2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that one Jabber Kha was the owner of the suit land under C.S. Khatian No.396 and S.A. Khatian No.12 in Plot Nos.590, 591,594, 663 and 664 total area of land amount 8.44 acres. The said Jabbar Kha on 05.03.1927 vide registered kabala No.288 transferred 5.60 acres of land in favour of Nizamuddin, Nazimuddin and Tamser Ali. Thereafter on 05.01.1924 vide registered kabala deed No.6623 transferred 5.65 acres of land to Nazimuddin, Nizamuddin and Kamoruddin. Then, due to the non-payment of rent/land revenue Bhawal Court of Wards Estate became the owner of this land vide Certified Case No.670 of 1929-30. Elahi Box, Nayon Box, Nizamuddin and Nazimuddin became the owner of 8.40 acres of land in equal share by auction purchase. Nazimuddin on 03.11.1940 sold his share in favour of Nizamuddin and Nayan Bee sold his entire share in favour of Elahi Box and S.A. Khatian No.1277 was correctly prepared in the name of heirs of Elahi Box and Nazimuddin for 8.40 acres of land and R.S. Khatian 127 showing 8.36 acres of land was recorded in the names of the plaintiff and co-owners. After the death of Nazimuddin his two sons namely, Faizuddin and Naziruddin and three daughters namely, Roushan Am, Mariam Begum and Lalbanu, and wife named Zamirunnessa became the owner of the land. Naziruddin died issue less and thus his brother, sisters and mother became the owner of his land. Zamiron Nessa on 15.01.1985 transferred 1.05 acres of land by Heba-bil-ewaz in favour of the plaintiff Nos.l-5. Roushan Ara on 19.03.1985 vide registered kabala No.3032 transferred 1.05 acres of land to the plaintiff Nos.1-3 and Lalbanu Vide registered kabala No.6112 dated 12/06/1990 transferred her land in favour of plaintiff Nos.1-3 and the heirs of Mariam on 08.08.2001 vide kabala No.7231 transferred their shares in favour of plaintiff Nos.l-3. Sirajul Haque and Ashia sold .35 acres of land to the plaintiff No.3, Shara Khatun, daughter Mariam on 13.08.2001 vide kabala No.7086 transferred their shares to the plaintiff Nos.1-3. After death of the plaintiffs' father the plaintiffs became the owners of 4.20 acres of land by law of inheritance and by purchase of properties by the predecessor of the defendant No.109, Tormaz Ali's name was recorded with recorded with the names of auction purchasers. The plaintiff with defendant Nos. 10-12 mutated 5.37 acres of land under same jama and paying the rents regularly and cultivating their respective land and planted trees and constructed houses therein and residing with their family members. Defendant Nos. 1-9 on 25.12.2001 tried to dispossess the plaintiffs, then the plaintiffs filed a proceedings under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Thereafter the said defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs form 10 decimals of land in plot No. 666 and hence the plaintiffs constrained to institute the instant suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. 

 4. Mr. Serajul Islam, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division did not consider that the appellant and others being plaintiffs earlier filed a suit for partition being Title Suit No. 6 of 2002 in respect of the land which also made the scheduled land in the instant case and the cunning respondent Nos. 1-7 with an ulterior motive after being informed about the earlier suit filed the instant suit on the basis of a forged auction bainanama in respect of the suit properly; that the appellant are the real owners of the suit property and it was concurrently found by both the Courts below that they have been possessing the suit land and the appellants being plaintiffs filed an earlier suit for partition before a civil Court but those were not considered by the High Court Division in giving it verdict in favour of the respondent Nos. 1-7. The learned Counsel further submitted that after issuance of the rule in the revision application and application for discharging the rule on ground of jurisdiction had been filed before the High Court Division alleging that there is no jurisdiction over the matter as both the original suit and the appeal were valued at Tk. 1,10,000.00 and obtained the Rule which had no pecuniary jurisdiction in disposing the matter. 

 5. It appears form the record that the trial Court discussed the evidence on record and the documents and also perused the documents and exhibits and also considered the material on record and made its clear observation and on the other hand the Court of Appeal below without applying its judicial mind and without considering the evidence on record and also by misreading the material evidence affecting the merit of the case came to a wrong and erroneous finding which is liable to be set aside. The Court of Appeal below while considering the evidence on record did not consider the material evidence particularly the evidence of P.W.3 who categorically stated in his evidence about the continuous possession of the plaintiff since long, in the suit land, who was not, cross-examined by the defendants. 

 6. The High Court Division observed that in the facts and evidence on record and legal position of the case the impugned judgment and decree dated 09.01.2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur, in Title Appeal No.241 of 2004 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing those dated 13.10.2004 passed the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur, in Title Suit No.17 of 2004 decreeing the suit was liable to be set 6- aside and the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court was affirmed.
